paragraphs: Scope and boundaries: this page covers only O*NET-SOC 19-1029.02 molecular and cellular biologists (studying cell molecules and organelles to understand cell function and organization), and does not cover adjacent occupations such as biochemists and biophysicists, microbiologists, medical scientists, bioinformatics pipeline maintenance, and natural sciences project management; laboratory operations, biosafety and chemical management, animal experimentation, and research ethics approval are determined by institutional and local rules.

How to judge: with a completely fictional experimental protocol and data table, check whether you can write the hypothesis, controls and replicates, sample and reagent registration, raw data records, statistical analysis methods, and limits of the conclusions, and list three check points and the handling of deviations; do only paper reasoning, without touching real patient samples, animals, or institutional biological materials.

What suits you: willing to ask questions about mechanisms, check data and records repeatedly against the protocol, withstand experimental failure and revise the hypothesis from it, and check before concluding when results are anomalous; note: if you dislike repeated recording and failed experiments, or tend to conclude directly from a single result, first compare adjacent directions.

Note: all of the following is editorially designed paper reasoning, without touching real samples, animals, or institutional research data, and it does not constitute laboratory operation, biosafety, chemical management, or research ethics authorization; any judgment involving safety, health, and qualifications must return to institutional procedures and local rules.

The official definition of molecular and cellular biologists (O*NET-SOC 19-1029.02, Molecular and Cellular Biologists) is: to study and explore cell molecules and organelles in order to understand cell function and organization; the scope excludes biochemists and biophysicists who study the chemical and physical principles of life processes, microbiologists who study microorganisms, medical scientists who study human disease and treatment, and bioinformatics technicians whose work is mainly data pipeline maintenance.

entries: Experimental design and execution: pose hypotheses about cell molecules and organelles, design molecular or cellular experiments and determine controls, replicates, and endpoint measures, supervise experimental execution, and interpret results.

Laboratory procedures and sample handling: complete procedures such as DNA sequencing, cloning and extraction, RNA purification, or gel electrophoresis according to protocols, register sample and reagent batches, and truthfully record raw data.
Raw records and data collection: maintain accurate laboratory records and data, registering samples, reagents, instrument parameters, and observations, and retaining versions and modification traces.

Data analysis and result interpretation: consolidate and analyze molecular or cellular experimental data, adjust the experimental design when necessary, and state the applicability, statistical limits, and uncertainty of the results.

Literature tracking and grant applications: track the field's literature and write grant applications to obtain research funding, preparing factual materials and budget explanations according to funder requirements.
Reporting and dissemination: prepare or review reports, papers, and conference presentations, accurately stating results, limits, and authorship boundaries.
Laboratory organization and teaching: coordinate laboratory activity priorities and teach undergraduate and graduate students in cellular or molecular biology.

paragraphs: Work context (O*NET Work Context survey): 92% of respondents use email every day, 88% work indoors in an environmentally controlled setting every day, and 81% wear common protective equipment every day (another 15% once a week or more); 54% consider exactness extremely important and 31% very important; 60% work more than 40 hours a week and 36% work 40 hours; 12% are exposed to disease or infection every day and 15% are in hazardous conditions every day; 46% say the degree of automation is slight, 27% moderate, and 23% not at all.

Ability focus: able to pose testable hypotheses and design controls and replicates, complete laboratory procedures according to protocols, maintain traceable raw records, complete statistical and graphical analysis, write clear scientific text, and check and report according to process when results are anomalous or deviations appear; requires knowledge of molecular biology, cell biology, and statistical methods, and habits of following biosafety and data integrity standards.

Preparation and training: O*NET lists this occupation at preparation level 5, usually requiring a doctorate or equivalent training; the education composition shows 35% bachelor's degree, 35% postdoctoral training, and 23% doctorate; the O*NET national training directory lists 4,580 higher education degree or certificate programs and lists no apprenticeship opportunities.

Occupational judgment: the key judgments are whether the hypothesis and controls hold, whether sample and reagent status is usable, whether the data are complete, whether the statistical methods apply, and whether the conclusion boundaries are accurate; when uncertain or beyond authorization, record and escalate first.

Main outputs: reproducible experimental protocols and raw data records, reviewable statistical and graphical analyses, papers and conference reports, grant applications, and progress and compliance reports submitted according to institutional requirements.

Conclusion: the core output of molecular and cellular biologists is reproducible experimental evidence and scientific explanation around the mechanisms of cell molecules and organelles; biochemists and biophysicists center on the chemical and physical principles of life processes, microbiologists on microorganisms themselves and infection processes, bioinformatics technicians on maintaining data pipelines and tools, medical scientists on human disease mechanisms and translational application, and natural sciences managers on project, personnel, and budget management. Adjacent relationships are used only for comparison and do not represent automatic transfer or mutual recognition of qualifications.

The comparison basis is the official O*NET 19-1029.02 description and tasks plus the O*NET profiles of adjacent occupations; it is an editorial summary and does not constitute a position recommendation.

Comparison dimensions: this page compares from three angles — the core work and outputs, the key difference from molecular and cellular biology, and what kind of choice each suits better — to help judge direction preference.

Difference from biochemists and biophysicists: this occupation focuses on the function and organization of cell molecules and organelles, mainly through cell-level experimental design; biochemists and biophysicists focus more on the chemical and physical properties of biological molecules and separation and characterization methods.

If you would rather study microorganisms themselves and infection processes, compare microbiologists; if you would rather do research at the species and ecosystem level, compare biologists; if you would rather do data pipelines and tool maintenance, compare bioinformatics technicians; if you would rather take on organizational coordination and management responsibility, compare natural sciences managers.
People studying for a degree or entering laboratory training

First become familiar with experimental record standards, biosafety, and equipment operation authorization, and complete basic laboratory procedures under mentoring, without skipping safety and ethics training.
Position staff mainly doing experimental execution and data collection
Include experimental protocol versions, sample and reagent numbers, instrument parameters, and raw data in traceable records, and report deviations and anomalies according to laboratory process.
Staff responsible for data analysis and result interpretation
Review conclusions with reviewable statistics and figures, distinguish hypothesis, observation, and inference, and have major conclusions confirmed by the project leader or an authorized person.
Career changers and cross-disciplinary people
First fill in molecular and cellular biology foundations, laboratory safety, and statistical methods, and accumulate reviewable analysis records using public datasets or simulated projects.

Boundaries: this checklist is an editorial summary and does not replace institutional biosafety, chemical management, animal experimentation, and research ethics procedures or local regulations; specific protection, exposure limits, and authorization follow competent-authority and institutional documents.

What most needs early judgment is non-reproducible experimental results, biological and chemical exposure, incomplete raw data and records, funding and position competition, long experiments and irregular schedules, and overreaching interpretation of results; different directions (experimental execution, data analysis, laboratory organization) have different exposure points.

Evidence scope: the work context proportions are the O*NET respondent framing (United States) and are not extrapolated to other regions; wages and employment use the broad framing labeled on the page; AI task exposure refers to ILO Working Paper 140 and NIST AI RMF 1.0.
Affected positions and tasks: staff responsible for cell culture and sample handling, chemical reagent preparation, data analysis, and conclusion writing.

Editorial risk scenarios: errors in records, samples, or conclusion control may trigger quality disputes; health controls follow the institutional risk assessment. Insufficient evidence: no research results on infection, chemical injury, retraction, or occupational stability for this occupation were obtained.

ai_impact_table.responsibility_intro: The steps below explain the order of human control when molecular and cellular biologists use tools: input checking, conditions of use, output review, and records.

responsibility_steps.说明: Check the experimental protocol, sample numbers, reagent batches, and instrument status, and confirm that the hypothesis, controls, and endpoint measures are clear.
Use tool assistance only when the protocol is approved, samples and data are traceable, and statistical methods are determined in advance.
Have a person review the raw data, statistical results, and figure sources, and do not directly accept tool-generated conclusions.
Record the protocol version, sample and reagent information, instrument parameters, raw data, and processing steps, and retain deviations and modifications.
Stop and report to the responsible person according to laboratory process when beyond the protocol, beyond authorization, or when results cannot be explained.

risk_rows.为什么重要: Conclusions cannot be attributed, and experiments and resources are wasted
risk_rows.控制方式: First clarify the hypothesis, controls, and endpoint measures, and start execution only after the protocol is reviewed

risk_rows.为什么重要: Results are not traceable and experiments must be redone
risk_rows.控制方式: Register samples and reagents by number and batch, record freeze-thaw and potency status, and have two people cross-check

risk_rows.为什么重要: Conclusions cannot be proven or pass an audit
risk_rows.控制方式: Record raw data and instrument parameters synchronously according to standards, and retain versions and modification traces

risk_rows.为什么重要: Experimenter health and laboratory safety risk
risk_rows.控制方式: Do a risk assessment for the specific materials and procedures, choose a suitable biosafety cabinet, chemical fume hood, and protection, which cannot be used interchangeably, and have the institutional safety officer confirm the controls and waste process.

risk_rows.为什么重要: Overinterpretation or erroneous inference entering the report
risk_rows.控制方式: Distinguish exploratory results from confirmatory conclusions, and have major conclusions confirmed by an authorized person before authorship
risk_rows.风险: Treating tool output as a conclusion

competence_ladder.description: Can complete basic laboratory procedures under mentoring according to protocol, truthfully record raw data, sample, and reagent information, and report anomalies.
Can independently design controls, execute molecular or cellular experiments, and complete statistical and graphical analysis, stating the applicability and limits of the results.

Can pose and lead research questions, supervise graduate students, and coordinate laboratory activities, but does not replace the institution's safety, ethics, and compliance signing responsibility.

risks.mitigation: Pre-set controls and replicates, register reagent batches and instrument status, record deviations, and review anomalous results according to process
risks.scenario: Unrecognized deviations in experimental conditions, reagent batches, or operations give inconsistent results for the same protocol across replicate experiments
risks.title: Non-reproducible experimental results

risks.affected_roles: Staff responsible for cell culture, chemical reagent preparation, and sample handling
risks.consequence: Editorial risk scenario: exposure to infectious or chemical materials must be assessed; the incidence of laboratory-acquired infection or injury in this occupation was not obtained, so assessment follows the specific procedure.
risks.mitigation: Choose isolation, cabinet type, and personal protection according to the CDC BMBL risk assessment principles and institutional procedures; a biosafety cabinet and a chemical fume hood are not interchangeable, and waste and exposure reporting are checked separately. | https://www.cdc.gov/labs/bmbl/index.html
risks.scenario: Insufficient protection and ventilation when handling infectious samples, cell cultures, organic solvents, or radioactive reagents
risks.title: Biological and chemical exposure

risks.affected_roles: Staff responsible for experimental records and data management
risks.consequence: Hard to prove conclusions or pass a data integrity review, affecting the credibility of results
risks.mitigation: Record raw data and processing steps synchronously according to standards, retain versions and modification traces, and check regularly
risks.scenario: Raw data, instrument parameters, and processing steps are not recorded synchronously, or modifications leave no trace
risks.title: Incomplete raw data and records

risks.affected_roles: Staff responsible for grant applications and dependent on project funding
risks.consequence: May affect project continuity and personal career stability and brings continuous time pressure
risks.mitigation: Build transferable skills and data assets, watch multiple funding channels, and declare truthfully according to institutional rules
risks.scenario: Depends on external funding with a limited number of positions; if an application is not funded, research progress and the position are affected
risks.title: Funding and position competition

risks.affected_roles: Staff responsible for cell culture, sampling, and instrument duty shifts
risks.consequence: Editorial suggestion: assess continuous duty shifts and rest arrangements; the O*NET NET60% working more than 40 hours a week does not prove fatigue, schedule-related illness, or attention decline outcomes for this occupation.
risks.mitigation: Arrange scheduling and rotation reasonably, record duty arrangements, and arrange rest according to the rules
risks.scenario: Cell culture, time-point sampling, and instrument runs require continuous duty, and the work week often exceeds 40 hours
risks.title: Long experiments and irregular schedules

risks.affected_roles: Staff responsible for data analysis, conclusion writing, and external communication
risks.consequence: May let erroneous conclusions enter reports, papers, or external statements and affect authorship responsibility
risks.mitigation: Distinguish exploratory from confirmatory conclusions, report uncertainty and limits, and publish major conclusions externally only after review
risks.scenario: Treating exploratory results or tool output as confirmatory conclusions and ignoring sample and statistical limits
risks.title: Out-of-bounds result interpretation

directions.fit_signals: Willing to do systematic experiments and verification around protein and nucleic acid mechanisms
directions.watchouts: Ignoring controls and replicates and concluding from a single result

directions.fit_signals: Willing to work on microbial culture, identification, and pathogenic mechanisms
directions.watchouts: Ignoring biosafety and strain management standards

directions.fit_signals: Willing to organize species and ecological data at a macro scale
directions.watchouts: Unwilling to handle field data and long-term observation records

directions.fit_signals: Willing to maintain data pipelines and review analysis results
directions.watchouts: Treating tool output directly as a conclusion

directions.fit_signals: Willing to conduct translational research on human disease questions
directions.watchouts: Ignoring clinical sample and ethics approval requirements

directions.fit_signals: Willing to coordinate research projects, personnel, and budgets
directions.watchouts: Ignoring front-line data quality and compliance requirements

personality_fit_block.heading: Fit signals, personality tool boundaries, and how to use them

questions.answer: Experimental design and hypothesis testing, laboratory procedure execution and deviation judgment, raw data and record standards, statistics and data analysis, literature reading and scientific writing, and habits of following biosafety and ethics standards.
questions.question: What abilities do molecular and cellular biologists mainly rely on?

questions.answer: No; ICR describes activity preferences only (Investigative, Conventional, Realistic), and fit should be judged from real research outputs, mentor feedback, and experimental records.
questions.question: Can the ICR interest code determine whether I am suited?

questions.answer: Checkable undergraduate laboratory training, rotation, or graduate training positions; the share of entry channels was not obtained. Real experiments require safety training and operation authorization.
questions.question: Can you enter the field without research experience?

questions.answer: It has little to do with extroversion or introversion; the key is consistent execution on data and records, patience with failed results, and cross-team collaboration and communication.
questions.question: Is an extroverted or introverted personality more suitable?

questions.answer: Job Zone5 is extensive preparation for the occupational group; 35% bachelor's / 35% postdoc / 23% doctorate are respondent answers about new-hire requirements, not the incumbent education ratio or a uniform doctorate entry requirement. Chinese position requirements are checked separately.
questions.question: What education, training, and qualifications are usually needed to enter the field?

questions.answer: No; the assessment is only for self-exploration, and hiring and qualifications should be determined by reviewable research outputs and institutional processes.
questions.question: Can assessment results serve as hiring or qualification evidence?

questions.answer: The O*NET work context shows that 60% work more than 40 hours a week and 35% consider competition extremely competitive; patience and recovery capacity should be part of self-assessment.
questions.question: Do long experiments and repeated failure strongly affect fit?

questions.answer: In the O*NET context, 12% are exposed to disease or infection every day and 15% to hazardous conditions; incidence rates cannot be inferred from context. Assess by material and procedure; a biosafety cabinet and a chemical fume hood are not interchangeable.
questions.question: Do laboratory chemical and biological exposures need attention?

questions.answer: Use public datasets or completely fictional data tables for paper analysis and reproduction exercises, retaining the analysis scripts, records, and limitation statements.
questions.question: How do you accumulate reviewable research evidence?

questions.answer: Start with literature reviews, public data reproduction, and paper experimental design, without using unauthorized patient samples, animals, or institutional biological materials.
questions.question: Which low-cost trials suit starting with?

signals.body: Willing to ask questions about mechanisms and check repeatedly against the protocol, sensitive to the consistency of data and records, and able to check before concluding when results do not match expectations.
signals.label: Fit signals

signals.body: Disliking repeated records and failed experiments, accepting only smooth results, or tending to conclude directly when data are incomplete.
signals.label: Signals requiring caution

signals.body: Complete one paper analysis with a public dataset or a completely fictional data table, writing out the hypothesis, controls, check points, and limitations.
signals.label: Low-cost trial

description.text: Molecular and cellular biologists (O*NET 19-1029.02) study the function and organization of cell molecules and organelles, designing molecular and cellular experiments and interpreting results. This page explains the official tasks and work context, the U.S. BLS 2025 Biological Scientists, All Other broad framing median wage of 98,920 USD and the 2024—2034 growth of 1%, the mainland China scientific research and technical services proxy wage, AI task boundaries, fit signals, and entry paths.

subject.name: Molecular and cellular biologists
subject.summary: Molecular and cellular biologists (O*NET-SOC 19-1029.02, Molecular and Cellular Biologists) study cell molecules and organelles to understand cell function and organization; the work is organized around designing and executing molecular or cellular experiments, completing laboratory procedures such as sequencing and cloning according to protocols, organizing and analyzing experimental data and interpreting results, and writing reports and grant applications.
